laws.rule: Cannabis Control Act, SNL 2018, c. C-4.1: nobody may consume cannabis in a public place, in a place where smoking is banned under the Smoke-free Environment Act, 2005, in or on a vehicle or boat, or in a place set by regulation (s. 75(1)). A vehicle or boat used as a dwelling is exempt while the vehicle is stationary on private land with the owner's permission, or the boat is moored or anchored (s. 75(3)). Nobody may possess more than 30 g of dried cannabis (or the federal equivalent) in a public place or in a vehicle in a public place (s. 64(1)). Nobody may drive or have care or control of a vehicle or boat, moving or not, with cannabis in it unless it is in its sealed purchase package, not readily available to anyone in the vehicle or boat, or the vehicle or boat is a dwelling (s. 77(1)). Under-19s may not enter a cannabis store (s. 74(3)).

The legal drinking age in Newfoundland and Labrador is 19: nobody may sell or give liquor to a person under 19 (Liquor Control Act, RSNL 1990, c. L-18, s. 76), and a person under 19 may not buy alcoholic liquor or enter a Newfoundland and Labrador Liquor Corporation store unless accompanied by a parent or guardian (s. 72). Possessing open alcoholic liquor in a public place is banned except under a licence or permit (s. 77(1)), and being intoxicated in a public place is an offence (s. 77(2)).

Nobody may drive or have the care or control of a motor vehicle, moving or not, with alcoholic liquor in it, unless it is in an unopened bottle or package with the seal unbroken, or packed with personal effects in fastened-closed baggage or otherwise not readily available to a person in the vehicle (Liquor Control Act, s. 80(1)). Separately, nobody may drive a motor vehicle in which someone is smoking when a person under 16 is in it, windows open or not (Smoke-free Environment Act, 2005, s. 6.1).

The Rooms, St John's: For booked photoshoots: no flowers, sessions on stairs, props/bags on floors or stairs, rearranging furniture or standing on it. Do not ask other visitors to move; keep noise and disruption low. These are The Rooms' conditions, not province-wide photography rules.

The Rooms, St John's: Ordinary gallery/exhibition non-flash photography is welcome unless an exhibition says otherwise. Separate amateur or professional photoshoot sessions must be booked in advance through the venue; maximum 30 minutes, check in 10 minutes early for an authorisation pass, handheld cameras only. Do not confuse this booked-session process with the ordinary permitted visitor photograph. Wider community/story permissions not yet checked.
The Rooms photography guidelines say alcohol is permitted only inside and served by The Rooms Café. This is the museum's own visitor/photography policy, not a provincial alcohol-law review.

items.text: The minimum age to buy or possess cannabis is 19. Adults may carry up to 30 g of dried cannabis (or equivalent) in a public place, and buy from stores licensed through the Newfoundland and Labrador Liquor Corporation (NLC) or NLC's online store. Buying or selling outside that system is an offence.

You can't use cannabis in a public place, a motor vehicle or a boat. Use is allowed in a private home or its yard, and may be allowed in a hotel room, an apartment or a rented campsite if the owner or operator permits (not in common areas). A vehicle used as a temporary or private residence may be an exception while it's parked off the road. Novice drivers, drivers under 22 and commercial drivers have zero tolerance for any detectable THC.

The legal drinking age is 19 (Liquor Control Act s. 72 and 76). You can't have open alcohol in a public place without a licence or permit, or be intoxicated in a public place (s. 77). In a motor vehicle, moving or not, alcohol must be unopened or packed away out of reach (s. 80).
